name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest hit; no famine declared
summary: El Niño drought cuts Sudan's harvest and raises famine risk; no drought famine declaration or exporter harvest failure
state: The IRC, citing the IPC alert of 13 Oct, says war and El Niño drought are compounding in Darfur and Kordofan, with nationwide harvests expected to be near record-poor and food stocks shrinking (IRC). In South Africa, El Niño points to a hotter, drier summer, but planting is progressing and a record 17.7 million tonne maize crop leaves ample stocks (Daily Maverick, 2 Nov). Severe drought in a major crop region keeps Watch; no new drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure was found as of 16 Nov.
for_you: Households in drought-hit parts of Sudan and southern Africa face higher food prices. Food importers and aid budgets are most exposed if El Niño cuts harvests in exporting regions over the coming season.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan) meets Watch; no famine declaration or exporter harvest failure for Alert

sources.title: IRC — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine
Daily Maverick — El Niño threatens SA's crops but ample maize stocks cushion the blow

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
